note_on_method: Nobody working on this has played on these courts. Everything below comes from the City of Vancouver's own pickleball page and, for one address, from the City's park page that corroborates it. This is a small set of three venues, and it is small because the City lists a fourth without a court count and with an address that its own park page contradicts. Publishing three and explaining the fourth is the honest shape of what Vancouver has written down.

slots.parking:
Not published, at any of the three. The City gives an address, a court count and, at Oakbrook, opening hours and a maintenance phone number, and says nothing anywhere about where to leave a car. Two of the three are community centres with their own car parks, which is a reasonable inference and not a stated fact, so it is not recorded as one.

Oakbrook Community Park sits just west of I-205 in a residential neighbourhood. Treat parking as unknown rather than assuming a lot.
slots.peak_hours:
Vancouver publishes no hourly demand figures, but Firstenburg Community Center's rules describe a busy room. Players must sign in on a sheet at the front desk, in person and only for themselves. Sign-in opens at 6 a.m. for morning pickleball, at noon for the afternoon, and thirty minutes before every other session. Wristbands are issued at sign-in and must be worn to be on court.

Once the maximum number of players has signed in, the session is marked FULL, and anyone arriving after that can pay the drop-in fee to join a waitlist that does not guarantee a game. Outdoors, the City asks players to rotate in using a paddle rack, and notes that scheduling apps do not reserve court time.
slots.surface_condition:
One surface is stated in the whole city: Firstenburg's six courts are on a wood gymnasium floor. Oakbrook and Marshall say nothing about what they are made of.

On condition, Vancouver does something no other operator in this directory does: it publishes a route for reporting a broken court. Both outdoor sites carry a maintenance line, 360-487-8177, and a link to the Public Works request form for Grounds service. That is not a statement about the state of the courts, and it is not recorded as one. It is a statement that somebody is responsible for them.
slots.local_scene:
Vancouver's pickleball is organised around its community centres rather than its parks. The adult leagues for ages 14 and up and the youth league for ages 10 to 14 all play at Firstenburg, and clinics run at both Firstenburg and Marshall.

The City also names the Columbia River Pickleball Club in an unusually practical way: at Fisher Basin Community Park, where nets are not provided, club members can reach club nets using a lockbox code. Oakbrook is the counterpoint, four courts with nets and poles permanently installed, so nothing needs organising at all.

best_for.heading: Best if you want to turn up and play outdoors
best_for.text: Oakbrook Community Park is the only outdoor pickleball in this set and it asks nothing of you: four dedicated courts, nets and poles permanently installed, open play for all skill levels, 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily, no reservations taken or possible. Bring a paddle. The one caveat is in the City's own words, that the courts do not have lighting, so those 10 p.m. hours are theoretical for much of a Pacific Northwest year.

best_for.heading: Best if you want the most courts under a roof
best_for.text: Firstenburg Community Center has six courts on a wood gymnasium floor, the largest pickleball room in the city and the home of every one of Vancouver's leagues. Play is free if you are a member of the community centre and costs a daily drop-in fee if you are not. The City states that the fee exists and never states what it is, so no number is printed here. Sessions run Monday to Friday for ages 12 and up and they do fill.

best_for.heading: Best if you are up before work
best_for.text: Marshall Community Center runs four indoor courts, and in high summer it runs them early: from 22 June to 22 August its pickleball hours move to 6 to 7:45 a.m., which the City explains is to keep dedicated court time without colliding with summer programming, in a cooler gym. It is a smaller room than Firstenburg and the same membership-or-drop-in arrangement applies.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts does Vancouver have?
faqs.a: We list 14 across three City of Vancouver venues: four outdoor at Oakbrook Community Park, six indoor at Firstenburg Community Center and four indoor at Marshall Community Center. The City lists a fourth site, Fisher Basin Community Park, without a court count, so it is not on this page.

faqs.q: Why is Fisher Basin Community Park not listed here?
faqs.a: Three reasons. The City states no court count for it, only that it has shared tennis and pickleball courts. Its address on the pickleball page is 3103 NE 99th Ave, which is Oakbrook Community Park's address, while the City's own park page for Fisher Basin gives SE 192nd Ave, Vancouver, WA 98607, in a different part of the city with a different postcode. And no published address for it carries a house number, so the Census geocoder returns no match.

faqs.q: Do any Vancouver courts have lights?
faqs.a: The City writes that Oakbrook's courts "do not have lighting", which is a stated negative, so Oakbrook reads No. Firstenburg and Marshall are indoor rooms where the question does not arise and the City says nothing, so both read "not stated".

At Oakbrook, we do not know. It is a City park with open-play courts that cannot be reserved, and it is very probably free, but the City never uses the word, so it is not printed here. At Firstenburg and Marshall, play is free for community centre members and visitors pay a daily drop-in fee whose amount the City does not publish.

faqs.q: Is this Vancouver, Washington or Vancouver, Canada?
faqs.a: Washington. This is Vancouver in Clark County, Washington, on the north bank of the Columbia River directly across from Portland, Oregon, not Vancouver, British Columbia, which is about three hundred miles further north and in another country. Portland's own eleven pickleball venues are a few miles away over the bridge and are published on this site too.
